issues.description: DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT duplicated rather than referenced from canonical source
issues.detail: Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat now declares its own `static final int DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT = 16;` while the writer (now in test sources) previously imported the same constant from `Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat`. Two definitions of the same physical constant in two packages is exactly the kind of silent drift hazard literate programming warns against: a future change to the on-disk block shift in one place will not propagate, and the only signal will be a corrupted segment. State the invariant in one place (the format module that actually owns the on-disk layout) and reference it; if the legacy code must be self-contained for module isolation, add a comment explaining that this constant must equal the original and why duplication was unavoidable.

issues.description: Dropped numMergeWorkers/mergeExec fields silently change constructor contract
issues.detail: The legacy `Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat` constructor still accepts `numMergeWorkers` and `mergeExec`, validates them, and then discards them (the fields were removed). Because `fieldsWriter` now throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, this is technically harmless at runtime, but the constructor's stated contract no longer matches its behavior: a reader who hasn't been told `this is read-only` will believe these arguments still influence merging. Either remove the parameters and route callers through a read-only constructor, or add a literate comment at the top of the class explaining that the arguments are accepted only for source/binary compatibility with code that still calls the old constructor and have no runtime effect.

issues.description: NAME constant downgraded from public to package-private may break external codec registries
issues.detail: `public static final String NAME` became package-private on both `Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat` and `Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat`. For a format identifier that has been part of the public API and is plausibly used by external tooling to identify segments on disk by name, this is a behavior-altering API narrowing dressed as a refactor. Audit: is anything outside the module (tests, tools, Elastic/OpenSearch downstreams) reading `NAME` reflectively or via direct reference? If yes, keep it public with `@Deprecated`; if no, document why the narrowing is safe in a one-line comment.

issues.description: Protected fields demoted to package-private without invariant audit
issues.detail: `OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues` had a long list of `protected final` fields that are now package-private (`final`). This is legitimate when no external subclass exists, but the class is `public abstract` and was previously designed for extension. The change quietly forecloses that extension point. Verify there are no out-of-tree subclasses (or callers in other Lucene modules) and, if the intent is to seal extension, mark the class non-public or add `sealed`-style documentation. The invariant being relied on here -- 'no one extends this outside the package' -- should be stated, not assumed.

issues.description: Reader-only legacy format lacks a literate comment stating the invariant
issues.detail: Both `Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat` and `Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat` now have `fieldsWriter` throwing `UnsupportedOperationException("Old codecs may only be used for reading")` with no class-level comment explaining the invariant. A careful reader picking this up cold sees a public class that extends `KnnVectorsFormat` but cannot actually write -- and has to infer the regime from a single thrown exception. Add a literate paragraph at the class javadoc: 'This format is retained in backward_codecs for *reading* segments produced by Lucene 9.9. Writing is intentionally unsupported; see Lucene104HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat. Test-only writer subclasses live in the test source set.' That single paragraph removes the puzzle.

issues.description: Two RW test formats (V0 and V1) with overlapping names invite future confusion
issues.detail: The diff renames `Lucene99RWHnswScalarQuantizationVectorsFormat` to `Lucene99RWV0HnswScalarQuantizationVectorsFormat` and adds `Lucene99RWV1HnswScalarQuantizationVectorsFormat`. The version suffix is meaningful (older writer vs current writer) but no single comment in the test source explains *what V0 and V1 actually correspond to* -- the only hint is `// this forces an older version of the writer` deep in an inner class. A literate-programming-grade three-line comment at each class -- 'V0 = pre-versioning writer; V1 = writer with VERSION_ADD_BITS; we keep both to exercise both on-disk shapes' -- would save the next reader an hour.

issues.description: VERSION_START / VERSION_ADD_BITS / VERSION_CURRENT not commented with on-disk semantics
issues.detail: The format keeps `VERSION_START = 0`, `VERSION_ADD_BITS = 1`, `VERSION_CURRENT = VERSION_ADD_BITS` as bare integers. For a legacy format whose entire purpose now is to be *read* correctly across versions, the version numbers and what each transition actually changed on disk should be stated next to the constants. Otherwise an engineer debugging a corrupted segment has to git-archaeology their way to the answer.

review.summary: The refactor is mechanically sound: a rename-and-relocate of the Lucene99 scalar-quantized formats to backward_codecs, with writers neutralized to throw UnsupportedOperationException and test-only RW subclasses re-providing write paths. Decision label: UNDER-AUDITED and NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT. The algorithms and on-disk layout are unchanged so there is no asymptotic risk, but the move introduces a duplicated DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT constant (silent-drift hazard for the on-disk block shift), accepts-and-discards constructor arguments without comment, and narrows several API surfaces (NAME, protected fields) without an explicit invariant statement. None of these are blockers for the move itself, but each one is a place where a careful reader has to reconstruct an invariant the code no longer states -- precisely the failure mode literate programming exists to prevent. A handful of short javadoc paragraphs at the class and constant level would convert this from a competent rename into one that the next maintainer can read without spelunking.
